title: Pairwise disjointness of Hamming spheres
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, let $u \in \alpha^n$ be a word of length $n$, and let $r$ be a natural number. For $t \in \bbn$, write $S_t(u)$ for the Hamming sphere of radius $t$ centred at $u$. Then the family $\{S_t(u)\}_{t \in \{0,1,\ldots,r-1\}}$ is pairwise disjoint: for any two distinct indices $s, t$ with $s, t < r$, the spheres $S_s(u)$ and $S_t(u)$ share no common word.
hypotheses_covered: finite alphabet with decidable equality (finite word type)
centre word u of length n
natural-number bound r indexing the family over {0,...,r-1}
replaced:
For any centre $u$ and bound $r$, the family $\{S_t(u)\}_{t < r}$ is pairwise disjoint
as a family of finsets indexed by $\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$.
